name: citelayer® – Agent Readiness | MCP Abilities, Schema.org
author: Saskia Teichmann

sections.description:
AI agents are starting to read websites the way browsers read them. They fetch a file, parse structured data, call a tool. If your site does not answer in a form they can use, they move on — and you never find out why.

citelayer® makes your WordPress site readable and usable for those agents, and tells you when something stops working. No coding, no configuration. Install, activate, done.

🔌 Works with AI Agents via MCP

citelayer® brings nine abilities to the WordPress Abilities API — seven of them registered out of the box, the two writing ones after you allow them (see below). Any MCP client that speaks to your site through the official WordPress MCP Adapter can then read your citelayer data instead of you copying it out of the dashboard by hand, and can run the two routine tasks below for you.

Seven abilities only read:

  • citelayer/get-readiness-score — the cached AI readiness score with every check
  • citelayer/get-llms-txt-status — llms.txt state, URL, listed and excluded posts
  • citelayer/get-bot-analytics — aggregated AI crawler traffic for 7, 30 or 90 days
  • citelayer/get-ai-blind-spots — published pages no AI bot visited
  • citelayer/get-referral-stats — visits arriving from AI assistants, by source
  • citelayer/get-schema-status — active Schema.org types and site identity completeness
  • citelayer/get-compatibility-status — detected SEO plugins and MCP availability

Two abilities change something:

  • citelayer/run-readiness-scan — runs the AI readiness checks and stores the result
  • citelayer/set-llms-txt-exclusion — includes a single post in llms.txt or holds it back

The two writing abilities are switched off out of the box. A new install and an update both start in Read-only mode: the seven reading abilities are available right away, the two writing ones do not appear in the client’s tool list at all, and a call that still arrives is refused. No update makes your site writable for an AI agent without you deciding so. To allow them, turn Read-only mode off under citelayer® → WebMCP.

Every ability requires an administrator account (manage_options), and the exclusion additionally requires the right to edit that particular post. The permission is checked twice: once before the call and once inside the ability itself, so a plugin that reaches the abilities through another route cannot skip it. Returns are aggregated: no IP addresses, no user agents, no e-mail addresses, no identity values.

The feature needs WordPress 6.9 or newer, since that is when the Abilities API landed in core. On older WordPress versions nothing is registered and nothing changes. citelayer® does not ship an MCP server of its own — transport is the adapter’s job — and you can switch all abilities off on the same page.

This exposes existing citelayer® data to tools you connect yourself. It does not influence whether or how AI systems cite your site.

🩺 Diagnosis — Find Out When It Breaks

Agent readiness is not a one-time setup. A caching layer, a server rule, another plugin or a stray static file can take an endpoint over from one day to the next, and nothing in the WordPress admin would tell you. citelayer® checks its own output and reports what it finds:

  • Endpoint diagnosis — calls /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and the Markdown routes the way an agent would, and compares the answer with what citelayer® generates internally. It tells apart a static file shadowing the route, an SEO plugin serving it with citelayer® additions merged in, a third generator, and a missing charset=utf-8 — so you get a cause, not just a red light
  • AI Readiness Scanner — ten checks with a score from 0 to 100, covering structured data, robots rules, Content-Signal headers, topic coverage, brand demand and, on shops, product content, images, stock and feed. The llms.txt endpoint is checked too, but not scored — see below
  • AI Blind Spots — published pages no AI bot has visited, so you can see which content never reached an agent at all
  • Compatibility status — which SEO plugin owns which output, and whether citelayer® merges into it or generates its own

🤖 AI Bot Analytics — Know Who’s Crawling Your Site

Track automated AI crawler requests and human AI referral visits separately. See which AI platforms send actual users to your site, and watch the bot traffic that’s discovering your content for those platforms.

  • 67 AI/LLM Bots Tracked — GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, DeepSeekBot, xAI-Bot, Meta-ExternalAgent, and 60 more
  • Real-Time Dashboard — Stat cards (7d/30d/90d/all-time), 30-day SVG trend chart, top bots leaderboard
  • AI Blind Spots — Discover pages invisible to AI bots with AI Discovery Score (0-100). Find and fix content gaps
  • Crawler Logs — Full log with filtering by bot, URL path, and date range. Paginated for large datasets
  • CSV Export — Download your bot data for offline analysis
  • Cache Plugin Detection — Auto-detects WP Rocket, LiteSpeed, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache. Provides setup guides to exclude AI bots from caching
  • 90-Day Auto-Cleanup — Keeps your database lean. No bloat, no maintenance
  • 100% Local — All data stored in your WordPress database. No external accounts, no API calls

📊 Schema.org — Structured Data That Supports the Rest

Automatically generates JSON-LD for your organization, site, articles and products, so an agent parsing your page finds the facts it needs in a form it already understands. Schema.org is supporting work here, not the centrepiece: citelayer® detects Yoast SEO, Rank Math and All in One SEO and merges its data into their markup instead of emitting a second block. If an SEO plugin is installed but not set up and produces nothing, citelayer® notices and supplies the markup itself.

📄 Serve Clean Content to AI Agents

When ChatGPT or Perplexity visit your page, citelayer® serves an optimized Markdown version instead of messy HTML. This uses 80% fewer tokens and gives AI a crystal-clear picture of your content.

🕒 Content Freshness

On a published post or page, citelayer® adds article:modified_time Open Graph metadata when a supported SEO plugin does not already provide it. The date describes the queried post or page. citelayer® does not set an HTTP Last-Modified header for generated HTML: the page can also include newer posts, menus or other content that changes without an edit to the queried post. The existing freshness option controls citelayer’s Open Graph output; other plugins, servers and caches manage their own HTTP validators.

🛡️ Stay in Control of Your Content

Configure how AI systems may use your content — allow or deny training, search indexing, and RAG/context usage. Your content, your rules.

🛒 Works with WooCommerce

If you run a shop, citelayer® makes your products visible to AI:

  • Product Schema.org markup generated
  • Product pages served as structured Markdown tables
  • AI agents can discover available shop capability status via UCP Discovery
  • Product data also listed in llms.txt

📄 llms.txt

citelayer® also generates an llms.txt (and optionally an llms-full.txt), the proposed convention for pointing AI systems at your content.

Be aware of what this is worth today. A study across 300,000 domains found no statistically significant difference in AI citation frequency between sites with and without llms.txt, and an analysis of 94,614 cited URLs found exactly one that pointed at a /llms.txt. citelayer® offers the file because the cost is near zero and the convention may still establish itself — not because it is known to have an effect. That is also why the AI Readiness Score no longer counts it at all — the check still runs and still shows you its status, it just does not move the number. The measurable parts of this plugin are the ones above.

📈 Why AI Visibility Matters Now

  • 58% of online searches will involve AI by the end of 2026
  • Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) are the next evolution of SEO
  • Sites without AI-readable content are invisible to ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and AI Overviews
  • citelayer® covers the readable side — the files, the markup, the abilities — and tells you when one of them stops working

✅ Free vs. Premium

The free plugin covers everything you need to get started:

✅ MCP abilities for the WordPress Abilities API (read-only out of the box)
✅ Endpoint diagnosis and AI Readiness Scanner with Topic Coverage and Brand Demand signal guidance
✅ Schema.org markup (Organization, WebSite, Article, Product)
✅ Markdown for AI agents
✅ Content-Signal headers
✅ WooCommerce product visibility in Schema.org, Markdown, and llms.txt
✅ llms.txt generation
✅ AI Bot Analytics (67 bots, dashboard, AI Blind Spots, CSV export)
✅ AI Referral Tracking (Visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, Mistral, Grok, and more)
✅ Cache plugin detection & setup guides

Premium adds:

🚀 WooCommerce add-on support for AI product discovery and controlled cart/checkout handoff
📈 AI Visibility Monitoring Dashboard
🔧 Advanced Schema.org (Reviews, FAQ, Shipping)
🛒 Product feed optimization

Full autonomous UCP shopping support is planned separately and is not claimed by the free plugin.

Learn more about Premium →

Get your AI Audit
citelayer® offers thorough AI Visibility Audits as a Service.
We help you become visible
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/citelayer/ or install via WordPress plugin installer
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress
  3. Go to citelayer → Dashboard in your admin sidebar to explore all features
  4. Visit /llms.txt on your site to verify output
  5. Check citelayer → Bot Analytics to see AI crawler activity (data appears automatically)
sections.faq:
Do I need technical knowledge to use this?

No. Install the plugin, activate it, and it works immediately. Bot tracking starts automatically in the background. There are optional settings if you want to fine-tune, but the defaults work great for most sites.

Will this help my site rank better in Google?

Yes! The Schema.org markup improves how search engines understand your content. Plus, as Google integrates more AI into search results (AI Overviews), having AI-readable content helps you appear in those new formats. citelayer® detects Yoast SEO and Rank Math to avoid duplicate Schema.

What is llms.txt, and is it worth anything?

llms.txt is a proposed convention, loosely modelled on robots.txt, for telling AI systems what a site is about and where its content lives. citelayer® generates one.

Honest answer on its value: the available studies find no effect. Across 300,000 domains there was no statistically significant difference in AI citation frequency between sites with and without the file, and in an analysis of 94,614 URLs cited by AI systems exactly one pointed at a /llms.txt. Treat it as a cheap bet on a convention that may still establish itself, not as something that gets you read today. The parts of this plugin you can actually measure are the MCP abilities, the structured data and the diagnosis.

How does Bot Analytics work?

citelayer® checks every incoming request against 62 known AI/LLM bot User-Agent strings. When a match is found, the visit is logged to a custom database table with timestamp, bot name, category, and URL path. This runs silently in the background — no configuration needed.

What are AI Blind Spots?

AI Blind Spots shows you pages on your site that have NOT been visited by any AI bot within a selected time period (7/30/90/365 days). Each page gets an AI Discovery Score (0-100) based on content length, title quality, excerpt, featured image, and age. Low scores indicate pages that need optimization.

Which AI bots does citelayer® track?

citelayer® tracks 67 AI/LLM bots from major providers:

  • OpenAI: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot
  • Anthropic: ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Claude-SearchBot
  • Google: Google-Extended, Gemini-Deep-Research, GoogleAgent-Mariner
  • Perplexity: PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User
  • Meta: Meta-ExternalAgent, Meta-ExternalFetcher, FacebookBot
  • xAI / DeepSeek / Mistral / Amazon / Cohere / HuggingFace and many more

Will this slow down my site?

Not at all. Bot detection adds less than 0.01 seconds per request. Dashboard stats are cached (5-minute transients). Everything else is aggressively cached — llms.txt refreshes every 24 hours, Schema every 7 days. AI-specific features only activate when an AI agent visits, not for regular users.

Does citelayer® track human visitors?

Bot Analytics logs identified AI/LLM bot requests. The AI Referrals tab also stores a minimal local event when a browser arrives with a known AI referrer or utm_source; this is used only to show AI click-through visits in your WordPress database. No external telemetry, accounts, or profiling are used.

What is GEO / AEO?

GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) and AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) are the next evolution of SEO. Instead of optimizing for Google’s blue links, you optimize for AI-generated answers. citelayer® handles the technical foundation so your content can appear in AI responses.

Can I control how AI uses my content?

Yes. citelayer® supports Content-Signal headers (contentsignals.org) that let you set rules:
* Allow or deny AI training on your content
* Allow or deny search indexing
* Allow or deny use in AI responses (RAG)

Default: Training denied, search and AI responses allowed.

What is UCP?

UCP (Universal Commerce Protocol) is an emerging commerce protocol for helping AI agents discover product and shop capabilities. The free plugin exposes discovery data; paid commerce add-ons can add product discovery and controlled cart/checkout handoff when enabled. Full autonomous UCP shopping support is planned separately and is not claimed by the free plugin.

Does citelayer® work with caching plugins?

Yes! Bot detection happens at the WordPress level before page caching. The Cache Config tab in Bot Analytics auto-detects WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, and WP Super Cache — and shows you exactly how to exclude AI bots from your cache for better tracking accuracy.

What happens to old bot data?

A daily cron job automatically deletes bot visit records older than 90 days to prevent database bloat. This is configurable via the citelayer_bot_analytics_cleanup_days filter.

1.13.5

  • FIX: Markdown frontmatter now keeps titles with colons, hash signs, quotes, backslashes, or line breaks as one valid YAML string in post and archive responses. Dynamic URLs and unexpected filtered dates are safely quoted; regular ISO dates keep their previous form. Markdown content and routes are unchanged; cached Markdown regenerates automatically after the update.

1.13.4

  • FIX: Stop setting a post-based Last-Modified HTTP header on generated HTML. Static pages can include newer posts or other changing content, so their own edit date is not a valid HTTP cache validator. Open Graph modified-time metadata remains SEO-plugin aware. Existing freshness settings are preserved.

1.13.3

  • FIX: Automatic text-route updates wait for a complete frontend request. Admin, AJAX, cron and CLI requests no longer mistake temporary provider differences for a changed site configuration.
  • FIX: Git download archives include valid production Composer metadata and load without excluded development packages; CI verifies the actual exported runtime.
  • FIX: Checking llms.txt status or removing a physical file no longer rebuilds WordPress rewrite rules unnecessarily. Fresh endpoint checks and file-removal safeguards remain.
  • FIX: Selective plugin loaders such as Freesoul Deactivate Plugins no longer let individual page requests change shared text-route migration state or remove saved compatibility modes. Genuine configuration changes still refresh the routes.
  • FIX: SEO compatibility detection follows the plugins loaded for each request, so returning to a full plugin profile restores the native llms.txt provider.
  • FIX: Root and well-known llms.txt addresses continue serving text when a selective loader omits their saved provider, while native output, explicit overrides and unrelated routes are preserved.

1.13.2

  • FIX: Easy Digital Downloads product feeds generate without WooCommerce installed, including scheduled regeneration.
  • FIX: Enabled /product-feed.xml endpoints return XML directly instead of WordPress trailing-slash redirects, while normal page redirects remain unchanged.

1.13.1

  • FIX: Prevent WordPress trailing-slash redirects for Citelayer-generated /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and /.well-known/llms.txt responses. Endpoint diagnostics now report redirect responses explicitly.
  • FIX: Rank Math Enhance mode preserves native llms.txt output when its handler is available and uses Citelayer otherwise. The well-known alias follows the same owner, and stored text routes refresh automatically after updates or ownership changes.
  • FIX: AI referral diagnostics explain the POST-only endpoint and the expected browser GET 404, and provide a read-only REST route index link.
  • FIX: Compatibility screens use locally installed SEO plugin icons or built-in WordPress icons, removing external icon requests.

1.13.0

  • NEW: Two writing citelayer abilities for the WordPress Abilities API — “citelayer/run-readiness-scan” runs the AI readiness checks and stores the result, “citelayer/set-llms-txt-exclusion” includes a single post in llms.txt or holds it back.
  • NEW: Every ability now carries an access level (read or write) and runs through a shared execution wrapper that checks the administrator capability a second time, so the permission callback is no longer the only barrier.
  • NEW: Toggle “Read-only mode” on the WebMCP settings page, on by default, so neither a new install nor an update makes a site writable for an AI agent without a deliberate decision. While it is on, the writing abilities are not registered at all and a call that still arrives is refused; the reading abilities are unaffected.
  • NEW: /.well-known/mcp/context.json now reports the read-only state and the access level of every registered ability.
  • IMPROVEMENT: An unexpected error inside an ability is returned as a WP_Error instead of escaping as an exception, so a single failure no longer empties an MCP client’s tool list.
  • IMPROVEMENT: The readiness scan started from an ability stops at a runtime budget instead of running into the PHP time limit, and reuses a recent result unless “force” is set. A scan that stops early keeps the previous scan timestamp, so the dashboard does not show a partial run as a fresh one and the next call can continue right away.
  • IMPROVEMENT: A completed ability scan now replaces the stored result instead of merging into it, so checks that no longer exist — for example the WooCommerce ones after deactivating WooCommerce — no longer linger in the score.
  • IMPROVEMENT: The citelayer ability category is described as “AI visibility data and controls”, since it is no longer read-only.
  • REMOVED: SEOPress is no longer detected or handled specially. citelayer treats it like any other SEO plugin it does not know. Four things change on a site with SEOPress active: citelayer’s own Schema.org markup stays on and is emitted next to SEOPress’s own markup, so the front page can carry the same entry twice; a post you marked noindex in SEOPress is no longer excluded from llms.txt and gets a Markdown version again; citelayer emits its own article:modified_time meta tag again, which appears twice if you switched on SEOPress’s “Display date in Google search results” option (it is off by default); and, if you never picked a Markdown scope yourself, citelayer now follows its own selection of post types instead of SEOPress’s sitemap, which can change which pages are served as Markdown. Your saved settings are untouched — only defaults that were derived from SEOPress being present. If you rely on SEOPress and want this back, please open an issue.
  • FIX: If an SEO plugin was installed but not set up — Rank Math before its setup wizard has run, or All in One SEO with schema markup switched off — citelayer held back its own Schema.org output while the SEO plugin produced none either, leaving the page with no structured data at all. citelayer now checks whether the SEO plugin actually outputs markup on the current request and steps in when it does not.

The schema status ability additionally reports how far the SEO plugin takes over.

short_description: Make your site readable and usable by AI agents: MCP abilities, structured data and a diagnosis that tells you when it breaks.
description:
AI agents are starting to read websites the way browsers read them. They fetch a file, parse structured data, call a tool. If your site does not answer in a form they can use, they move on — and you never find out why.

citelayer® makes your WordPress site readable and usable for those agents, and tells you when something stops working. No coding, no configuration. Install, activate, done.

🔌 Works with AI Agents via MCP

citelayer® brings nine abilities to the WordPress Abilities API — seven of them registered out of the box, the two writing ones after you allow them (see below). Any MCP client that speaks to your site through the official WordPress MCP Adapter can then read your citelayer data instead of you copying it out of the dashboard by hand, and can run the two routine tasks below for you.

Seven abilities only read:

  • citelayer/get-readiness-score — the cached AI readiness score with every check
  • citelayer/get-llms-txt-status — llms.txt state, URL, listed and excluded posts
  • citelayer/get-bot-analytics — aggregated AI crawler traffic for 7, 30 or 90 days
  • citelayer/get-ai-blind-spots — published pages no AI bot visited
  • citelayer/get-referral-stats — visits arriving from AI assistants, by source
  • citelayer/get-schema-status — active Schema.org types and site identity completeness
  • citelayer/get-compatibility-status — detected SEO plugins and MCP availability

Two abilities change something:

  • citelayer/run-readiness-scan — runs the AI readiness checks and stores the result
  • citelayer/set-llms-txt-exclusion — includes a single post in llms.txt or holds it back

The two writing abilities are switched off out of the box. A new install and an update both start in Read-only mode: the seven reading abilities are available right away, the two writing ones do not appear in the client’s tool list at all, and a call that still arrives is refused. No update makes your site writable for an AI agent without you deciding so. To allow them, turn Read-only mode off under citelayer® → WebMCP.

Every ability requires an administrator account (manage_options), and the exclusion additionally requires the right to edit that particular post. The permission is checked twice: once before the call and once inside the ability itself, so a plugin that reaches the abilities through another route cannot skip it. Returns are aggregated: no IP addresses, no user agents, no e-mail addresses, no identity values.

The feature needs WordPress 6.9 or newer, since that is when the Abilities API landed in core. On older WordPress versions nothing is registered and nothing changes. citelayer® does not ship an MCP server of its own — transport is the adapter’s job — and you can switch all abilities off on the same page.

This exposes existing citelayer® data to tools you connect yourself. It does not influence whether or how AI systems cite your site.

🩺 Diagnosis — Find Out When It Breaks

Agent readiness is not a one-time setup. A caching layer, a server rule, another plugin or a stray static file can take an endpoint over from one day to the next, and nothing in the WordPress admin would tell you. citelayer® checks its own output and reports what it finds:

  • Endpoint diagnosis — calls /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and the Markdown routes the way an agent would, and compares the answer with what citelayer® generates internally. It tells apart a static file shadowing the route, an SEO plugin serving it with citelayer® additions merged in, a third generator, and a missing charset=utf-8 — so you get a cause, not just a red light
  • AI Readiness Scanner — ten checks with a score from 0 to 100, covering structured data, robots rules, Content-Signal headers, topic coverage, brand demand and, on shops, product content, images, stock and feed. The llms.txt endpoint is checked too, but not scored — see below
  • AI Blind Spots — published pages no AI bot has visited, so you can see which content never reached an agent at all
  • Compatibility status — which SEO plugin owns which output, and whether citelayer® merges into it or generates its own

🤖 AI Bot Analytics — Know Who’s Crawling Your Site

Track automated AI crawler requests and human AI referral visits separately. See which AI platforms send actual users to your site, and watch the bot traffic that’s discovering your content for those platforms.

  • 67 AI/LLM Bots Tracked — GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, DeepSeekBot, xAI-Bot, Meta-ExternalAgent, and 60 more
  • Real-Time Dashboard — Stat cards (7d/30d/90d/all-time), 30-day SVG trend chart, top bots leaderboard
  • AI Blind Spots — Discover pages invisible to AI bots with AI Discovery Score (0-100). Find and fix content gaps
  • Crawler Logs — Full log with filtering by bot, URL path, and date range. Paginated for large datasets
  • CSV Export — Download your bot data for offline analysis
  • Cache Plugin Detection — Auto-detects WP Rocket, LiteSpeed, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache. Provides setup guides to exclude AI bots from caching
  • 90-Day Auto-Cleanup — Keeps your database lean. No bloat, no maintenance
  • 100% Local — All data stored in your WordPress database. No external accounts, no API calls

📊 Schema.org — Structured Data That Supports the Rest

Automatically generates JSON-LD for your organization, site, articles and products, so an agent parsing your page finds the facts it needs in a form it already understands. Schema.org is supporting work here, not the centrepiece: citelayer® detects Yoast SEO, Rank Math and All in One SEO and merges its data into their markup instead of emitting a second block. If an SEO plugin is installed but not set up and produces nothing, citelayer® notices and supplies the markup itself.

📄 Serve Clean Content to AI Agents

When ChatGPT or Perplexity visit your page, citelayer® serves an optimized Markdown version instead of messy HTML. This uses 80% fewer tokens and gives AI a crystal-clear picture of your content.

🕒 Content Freshness

On a published post or page, citelayer® adds article:modified_time Open Graph metadata when a supported SEO plugin does not already provide it. The date describes the queried post or page. citelayer® does not set an HTTP Last-Modified header for generated HTML: the page can also include newer posts, menus or other content that changes without an edit to the queried post. The existing freshness option controls citelayer’s Open Graph output; other plugins, servers and caches manage their own HTTP validators.

🛡️ Stay in Control of Your Content

Configure how AI systems may use your content — allow or deny training, search indexing, and RAG/context usage. Your content, your rules.

🛒 Works with WooCommerce

If you run a shop, citelayer® makes your products visible to AI:

  • Product Schema.org markup generated
  • Product pages served as structured Markdown tables
  • AI agents can discover available shop capability status via UCP Discovery
  • Product data also listed in llms.txt

📄 llms.txt

citelayer® also generates an llms.txt (and optionally an llms-full.txt), the proposed convention for pointing AI systems at your content.

Be aware of what this is worth today. A study across 300,000 domains found no statistically significant difference in AI citation frequency between sites with and without llms.txt, and an analysis of 94,614 cited URLs found exactly one that pointed at a /llms.txt. citelayer® offers the file because the cost is near zero and the convention may still establish itself — not because it is known to have an effect. That is also why the AI Readiness Score no longer counts it at all — the check still runs and still shows you its status, it just does not move the number. The measurable parts of this plugin are the ones above.

📈 Why AI Visibility Matters Now

  • 58% of online searches will involve AI by the end of 2026
  • Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) are the next evolution of SEO
  • Sites without AI-readable content are invisible to ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, and AI Overviews
  • citelayer® covers the readable side — the files, the markup, the abilities — and tells you when one of them stops working

✅ Free vs. Premium

The free plugin covers everything you need to get started:

✅ MCP abilities for the WordPress Abilities API (read-only out of the box)
✅ Endpoint diagnosis and AI Readiness Scanner with Topic Coverage and Brand Demand signal guidance
✅ Schema.org markup (Organization, WebSite, Article, Product)
✅ Markdown for AI agents
✅ Content-Signal headers
✅ WooCommerce product visibility in Schema.org, Markdown, and llms.txt
✅ llms.txt generation
✅ AI Bot Analytics (67 bots, dashboard, AI Blind Spots, CSV export)
✅ AI Referral Tracking (Visits from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, DeepSeek, Mistral, Grok, and more)
✅ Cache plugin detection & setup guides

Premium adds:

🚀 WooCommerce add-on support for AI product discovery and controlled cart/checkout handoff
📈 AI Visibility Monitoring Dashboard
🔧 Advanced Schema.org (Reviews, FAQ, Shipping)
🛒 Product feed optimization

Full autonomous UCP shopping support is planned separately and is not claimed by the free plugin.

Learn more about Premium →

Get your AI Audit
citelayer® offers thorough AI Visibility Audits as a Service.
We help you become visible
